results.summary: This design implements a single XOR gate and an inverter on a Tiny Tapeout tile. Inputs ui[0] and ui[1] feed the XOR, whose output appears on uo[0], while uo[2] and uo[3] provide inverted outputs. The project is intended as a basic logic gate test and includes a truth table for verification. It was created using the Wokwi editor and has no external hardware requirements.

This chip implements a simple AND gate and an OR gate, with eight inputs and two outputs. It was created as a template for a University of Toronto hackathon event to demonstrate basic logic gates. The design is tested by toggling inputs A, B, and C and observing the outputs. A seven-segment display is listed as external hardware, though the documentation does not explain how it is connected.

This design uses NOT, NOR, and NAND gates to generate output patterns that represent the ASCII letter A. A single input ui[0] drives the logic chain, and the outputs uo[0] and uo[1] produce high/low levels that can be viewed on an LED array or logic analyzer. The project is intended as a basic logic gate test and requires no external hardware. It operates at a clock frequency of 10 kHz.

This design chains seven XNOR gates, each combining the previous gate's output with a new input. It has eight inputs and eight outputs, with the outputs producing varying displays based on the input pattern. The documentation is minimal and does not clearly explain the intended function beyond the gate chain. It was created in Wokwi and has no specified external hardware.

This design detects and sorts signals from two groups of two units each, indicating whether a partial or full signal is present in each group. It takes four inputs and produces four outputs that encode the signal status. The circuit is intended for error or failure reporting and is tested by simulating in Wokwi with DIP switches. No external hardware is required.

This design uses a button and switches to control a seven-segment display and LEDs. When switch 1 is on, the display shows a 7; pressing the button also shows a 7 but with a different appearance. Switch 2 halves a value so that only one LED segment is lit. The project is a simple test of inputs and outputs, created in Wokwi, and requires a push button, a seven-segment display, and an 8-position DIP switch as external hardware.

This design implements a collection of basic logic gates including AND, OR, XOR, and NOT, with eight inputs and eight outputs. The documentation is sparse and does not describe the specific gate connections or intended function beyond listing the inputs. It is tested by toggling the eight inputs and observing the outputs. The project was created in Wokwi and has no external hardware requirements.

This design implements one AND gate and two OR gates, with six inputs and five outputs. The AND gate uses inputs a and b, while the OR gates use separate input pairs. The project is a basic logic gate test, created in Wokwi, and is tested by setting inputs high and observing the corresponding outputs. No external hardware is specified.

This design implements a full adder using AND, OR, and XOR gates. It takes three inputs (a, b, and carry-in) and produces sum and carry-out outputs on uo[0] and uo[1]. The project is a simple educational demonstration of adder logic, created in Wokwi, and is tested by toggling switches. A seven-segment display is listed as external hardware, though its connection is not detailed.

This design implements a mix of AND, NAND, and OR gates, with eight inputs and eight outputs. Some outputs are directly connected to inputs, while others come from the logic gates. The documentation is minimal and does not clearly describe the overall function or how the gates are interconnected. It was created in Wokwi and has no specified external hardware.
